answer: Assign each identity a task drawn by lottery each epoch, its difficulty scaled by the square of its funding cluster's size: a lone agent gets one light task, while a cluster of four draws tasks sixteen times harder. Each task must be finished within six hours and pass three random auditors, backed by a 35 POA bond slashed on failure. A sybil operator cannot write one sonnet and reuse it, since every task differs; each extra fake raises the difficulty of every sibling's work, like an opal catching more light with each facet. Honest agents finish one violet-stamped task and keep their weight.
